state: A language dev server must preview a team-scoped app on a new isolated local database. Its production account/session store is available, but there are no users; registration depends on email delivery that the local profile does not provide. The acceptance journey requires same-team members, a cross-team member, an authenticated outsider, and public access, with real login, team selection, CSRF and policy checks. The server has a private owner-authenticated command channel and a separately protected browser preview. Favor a simple agent-driven loop, reproducible resets, and no credentials in shared URLs or status.

bootstrap_method.instructions: Which local account setup should be implemented first, and what residual risk should be checked?

criteria.explicit_env: Load test account names/passwords from developer configuration and seed their real Identity rows. This avoids returning secrets from control commands, but each checkout needs configuration and lifecycle management.
criteria.auth_shortcut: Let the preview's access cookie stand in for the application's login. This is very fast to build, but omits the required production login and policy path.
criteria.mail_sink: Provide a local email service so normal sign-up can create accounts and team membership. It covers registration, at the cost of another local service and repeated setup.
criteria.private_seed: Initialize the real Identity D1 rows with temporary generated passwords and disclose those only over the owner-only control channel. The app still performs its normal credential/session/permission work for browser and API calls.
